summary: Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1963 as lecturer, 1973–1987 as committee member) and served as representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He held posts at Komazawa, Japan Women's University, and the University of Tokyo (1912, 1918–1930).
Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University. He held an assistant professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D. 1994). He served at Koyasan University as an assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and later as professor (attested 2005).
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1933. He later served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1900) and the University of Tokyo (~1900–1906).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Taisei Iwata works in Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 1996).
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kodo Sawaki (~1936–1965) and founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo (MA 1961), later serving as professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2005) and concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).
Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University (~1934–1937), where he later served as director (~1962–1978).

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo (MA, PhD), and held the Jill Ker Conway Professorship of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).
Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1949–1953) and under Mumon Yamada (~1953–1988). He served as president of Hanazono University (~1993–2001).

Taixu (1890–1947) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jichan, Jingan, and Yang Renshan. A monk at Bilu Temple (~1911–1912), he led the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded several institutes, including Minnan and Wuchang.

Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) studied Buddhism, literature, and philosophy under Baian Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, and at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and SFSU. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956) and founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles.
Tak Pui Sze works in Sinology and religious studies. Sze earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen.

Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Japan Women's University (~1945–1949) and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1982–1988).

Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2015, Kameyama served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
